chunks: And in the narration of Ismāʿīl ibn Muslim, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, peace be upon him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said:

The back may be ridden when it is pledged, and the maintenance of it is upon the one who rides it. And the milk may be drunk when it is pledged, and the maintenance is upon the one who drinks the milk.

key_terms.اَلظَّهْرُ: the back of a riding animal, meaning its riding use
key_terms.مَرْهُونًا: given as collateral or pledged security

ai.seo_question: Can a pledged animal be ridden or its milk consumed in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling regarding pledged property: the benefit of a pledged riding or milking animal may be used under specific circumstances. The one who takes such benefit is responsible for the animal’s maintenance and expenses.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4095 - In a narration from Ismail ibn Muslim, from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) from his father, Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), from his forefathers (peace be upon them), from Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as), who said that the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace be upon him and his family) said:

"The back (of a riding animal) may be ridden if it is given as collateral (rahn), and the one who rides it is responsible for its expenses.
And the milk may be drunk if it is given as collateral, and the one who drinks the milk is responsible for its expenses."
